meta.notes: Default result, repair limits by type, energy comparison and cross-check for the repair-or-replace tool. Replacement prices are equipment only until labor data is added.

defaultInputs.note: Example inputs for the server-rendered default result; not data about any real home.

default.headline: Repair is possible, but the quote is high for a young heater
default.explain: At 8.0 years it has used 62% of a 13-year typical life. The repair is 28% of the replacement price, more than 25%. Get a second quote, or ask what else is worn before you decide. If you replace it, a high-efficiency ENERGY STAR gas tank (UEF 0.9) would cost about $77 a year less to run than a standard gas tank.
default.formula:
Expected life (gas tank) = 13 years; "old" from 0.75 × 13 = 9.8 years
Life used = 8.0 ÷ 13 = 62%
Repair share = $250 ÷ $899 = 28%
Rules: leak or flood → replace; share > 50% → replace; old and share > 25% → replace; old → borderline; share > 25% → borderline; else repair
Running cost (55 gal/day, 67 °F rise): Gas tank UEF 0.635 = $262/yr; Gas tank (high efficiency, ENERGY STAR) UEF 0.9 = $185/yr; difference $77/yr
default.sources: Rules: ours, stated on /methodology. Typical life: DOE (13 years for tanks, 20 for tankless). New-unit price: typical equipment price from Home Depot listings (2026-11-12), before installation; type your installed quote if you have one. See our rules checked against Rheem and A. O. Smith guidance.

symptoms.label: Water leaking from the tank itself
symptoms.note: A leak from the tank body cannot be fixed; the heater has to be replaced. Check first that the water is not coming from a pipe, valve or fitting above it, because leaks are often in the plumbing, not the heater.

symptoms.label: Drip at a valve, pipe or fitting
symptoms.note: Small valve or fitting leaks are often repairable.

symptoms.label: Rusty or discolored hot water
symptoms.note: Rheem lists rusty or discolored hot water as a sign the heater should be replaced. Rusty water can also come from old pipes, so check whether the cold water is clear.

symptoms.label: Rumbling or popping noise
symptoms.note: Persistent rumbling or popping comes from hardened sediment on the tank floor; Rheem counts it among the signs of replacement.

symptoms.label: No hot water, or not enough
symptoms.note: Often a heating element, thermostat or (on gas units) the ignition parts. Heating elements, thermostats and anode rods are designed to be replaced.

symptoms.label: Relief valve dripping or discharging
symptoms.note: The temperature and pressure (T&P) relief valve is a safety device. Never cap or plug it or its discharge pipe; have the cause checked.

symptoms.label: Heater was in a flood
symptoms.note: If the heater was flooded or its controls were under water, the manufacturer says the whole unit must be replaced.
